test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two observers stand 100 meters apart and observe the top of a tower. The angles of elevation are 30° and 45°. Find the height of the tower (assuming both observers are on the same side of the tower).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Closer observer has larger angle = 45°, so height = distance from tower.

Let nearer distance = x ⇒ height = x

Farther distance = x + 100

tan30° = h ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3

x ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3 ⇒ x = 100 ÷ (√3 − 1)

**∴ Answer = 50(√3 + 1) m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between observers = 100 m

Angles of elevation = 30°, 45°

Both on same side of tower

**Formula used:**

tanθ = height ÷ base

 
• 
• h 45° 30° 
• 
• 
• 100 m 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let distance of nearer observer = x

⇒ tan45° = h ÷ x ⇒ 1 = h ÷ x ⇒ h = x

⇒ Distance of farther observer = x + 100

⇒ tan30° = h ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3

⇒ x ÷ (x + 100) = 1 ÷ √3

⇒ √3x = x + 100 ⇒ x(√3 − 1) = 100

⇒ x = 100 ÷ (√3 − 1) = 50(√3 + 1)

**∴ The correct answer is 50(√3 + 1) m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angles of Elevation Concept

Angle between horizontal and line of sight. tanθ = height ÷ base is most useful relation.

Same Side Observation Rule

Distance difference is directly added: farther distance = nearer distance + separation.

Standard Values

tan30° = 1 ÷ √3, tan45° = 1 — frequently used in height-distance problems.

Rationalization Trick

1 ÷ (√3 − 1) = (√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1) = (√3 + 1) ÷ 2 for faster simplification.
